overview.text: The California Whipsnake (Striped Racer) is a fast, slender, non-venomous snake of California and Baja California.

identification.text: Slender, dark brown or black on top with a yellowish stripe along each side.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: California west of the Sierra Nevada, from Trinity County south, and north-western Baja California.

behaviour.text: Fast and active by day, moving through brush and up into bushes to bask in the morning sun.

diet.text: Insects, lizards, snakes, birds and small mammals, but especially lizards, which it grabs and swallows alive.

reproduction.text: Hibernates from November to February, mates in spring and lays 6 to 11 eggs.

recognise.text: Yellow side stripe on a dark, slender body.
